stem: Madhav meets the compact writings $3p$ and $9(z+5)$ in his algebra notebook.

parts.text: How should he read them before any calculation?

options.text: $3p$ means $3 \times p$, and $9(z+5)$ means $9$ times the whole of $(z+5)$.
$3p$ names an omitted multiplication sign as a new letter, not three times $p$.
The value is whichever numeral appears first in the writing.
$3p$ still means multiplication even if the letter stands alone with no numeral beside it.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A number next to a letter means multiplication, and a number next to brackets multiplies the whole grouped expression inside.

teacher.key_rationale: Compact notation 3p is 3×p and 9(z+5) multiplies the whole bracket. B mislabels the omitted sign. C grabs the first numeral. D drops the coefficient condition.
